newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields, zloty to consolidate next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields, zloty to consolidate next week.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to consolidate at next Tuesday's primary auction and the zloty is seen holding on to this week's gains against the basket of currencies in the coming week, analysts said on Friday.

They said the recent growth trend in treasury yields, caused by uncertainty over next year's inflation amid infighting within Poland's ruling coalition about 1997 tax levels, would likely be put on hold at Tuesday's tender.
"T-bill yields will certainly not fall but their upward move is likely to be held in check by the finance ministry," said Rafal Chodzidlo, senior dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
On Tuesday the treasury will offer 1.2 billion zlotys of T-bills, including 700 million of its benchmark 52-week paper.

Analysts said the treasury may have to cut the minimum price of the benchmark, last at 83.52, by one grosz because of the relatively large offer, but minimum prices of the 13- and 26-week papers were likely to remain flat at 95.50 and 91.15.
"The treasury is likely to cut the minimum price only for the benchmark," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.
Due to a market holiday on Polish Independence Day on Monday the weekly tender was moved to Tuesday and the value date to Thursday, November 14, not Wednesday as usual.
Analysts said foreign investors were likely to refrain from any major T-bill purchases before the situation with next year's tax levels was cleared up.

"Foreign investors seemed to have switched their focus from 52-week T-bills to (16-percent fixed) two-year bonds, but I don't believe they will be active before 1997 taxes are set," said Slawomir Soroczynski of Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA.

Next week Poland's upper house of parliament is due to vote on whether to amend a 1997 tax bill passed by the lower house, which envisiges the creation of an aditional, lower, fourth tax bracket for the poorest.
A Senate committee recommended to the full uppper house earlier this week to adopt a three-stage tax scale but with different levels than those proposed by the government.

Late in October the lower house, Sejm, unexpectedly passed a four-level tax bill, when the coalition's smaller Peasant party backed a opposition motion vehemetly opposed by the government and the largest ex-communist party.

The government, which this week signalled it may resign if the four bracket tax plan came into law, said the Sejm's sheme would curb budget inflows next year, increase the budget gap and fuel inflation.
The Polish zloty, which this week firmed 0.25 percentage point versus the currency basket to above two percent from the parity rate, was seen consolidating its gains next week.
"Zloty consolidation around two percent from parity is likely, with resistance around 2.15 and support around 1.9 percent," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

Analysts said the zloty's upward shift from its week's old trading band of 1.6 to 1.9 percent from parity was caused mainly by the weakness of the U.S. dollar on world market this week amid nearly no zloty-depressing importers' orders.
The Polish currency closed at 2.8090/05 per dollar and at 1.8607/15 per mark, or about 2.10 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than the previous Friday's 1.85 percent close.
The money market was seen remaining balanced next week with one-day deposit rates floating around the central bank's main 14-day reverse repo rate, last at 19.14 percent. @
"One-day rates exactly straddled the central bank reverse repo on Friday and I expect them to stay at 19.10/19.20 percent next week," said Elwir Swietochowski from PBI SA.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
